# Minimal same-device FF-up diagnostic: packet12 source review

**No installed route can run this diagnostic on the current server.** A future sealed extension and one controlled application reload are required. Do not edit the live frozen source or use the compiler modes as an arbitrary callback mechanism. This review issued no native imports, endpoint calls or runtime mutations. The earlier output-partition audit's fault-halted status is historical; root owns current campaign and health assessment.

Packet12 provides final-output capture (`LTXBaselineCapture`: images, video/audio latents, waveform), fixed one-/multi-block compiler gates, and an identity HTTP route. The compiler gates clone actual block inputs transiently and retain shape/state metadata and output hashes. Their backend writes FX Python and rewrite metadata; `example_inputs` is consumed by compilation and is not a raw-input archive. None exposes persistent values at the FF-up Linear boundary. Final latents cannot reconstruct those values. The compiler adapters explicitly reject additional module hooks, so attaching a Linear hook to an existing compiled candidate would violate their guards.

The smallest future test is one original-graph request with a dedicated diagnostic node selecting only `transformer_blocks[24].ff.net[0].proj`, retaining the original transformer/registration/routing. The module's BF16 weight is `[16384,4096]`, bias absent, on XPU1. The input to capture is **after** the original video RMS/adaptive modulation, directly at this projection. Source-inferred stages are `[1,64,4096]` then `[1,256,4096]`; observe actual dtype/device/stride and bytes rather than treating block-input metadata as a Linear-input capture.

A narrowly scoped per-instance forward observation hook is one possible new adapter: observe the actual native full-N result, compare an isolated original-operation repeat and `cat(linear(x,W[:8192]), linear(x,W[8192:]), dim=-1)` on XPU1, and return the original result unchanged. Keep the full K reduction, order of halves and original GELU/down-projection/residual sequence. Use the exact Comfy effective-weight context where applicable; reject training, quantization, weight/bias functions, low-VRAM transformations, nonresident state and foreign hooks. First require the isolated full-N call to match the observed original module output, then compare both half calls and their repeat bytewise, including signed zero; stop on the first mismatch. A direct call with `module.weight` is insufficient if it bypasses active cast/transform semantics.

Bound diagnostics to the first invocation of each stage (calls1 and9 of the existing eight-plus-three sampler schedule), count all11 observed projection calls, remove the exact owned hook in a guarded cleanup, and refuse owner/registration changes or repeated admission. Pin sources, model/server identity, deterministic state and target storage before/after. Preserve only these two actual input captures plus native outputs and mismatch evidence, with explicit bounded retention. Optional full BF16 weight export is128MiB; original pinned checkpoint identity plus selected-weight hash avoids requiring an extra persistent weight copy. Half-row views avoid weight replicas for this same-device test; output/check copies and any raw archive still need explicit memory accounting.

This diagnostic intentionally adds work and CPU evidence transfers, so its clip timing cannot establish a speedup. Require both stage operator gates and all four original raw clip outputs before considering a later true candidate. Cross-device execution, remote ownership, stream synchronization and wider layer selection remain separate future work. No installed-source change, general probe framework or native experiment was performed here.

Exact inspected packet/source pins are in `data/ltx-linear-same-device-route-review-01.json`.
